stories.summary: Singapore's economy grew 6.1% in the third quarter from a year earlier — above the 5.4% advance estimate and the 5.6% Reuters poll — and the government raised its 2026 growth forecast to around 6%, from 4.5% to 5.5% in August. Growth in 2027 is expected at 2.5% to 4.5%, and Enterprise Singapore lifted its 2026 non-oil domestic exports forecast to 30% to 32%, driven by AI-related electronics and machinery.
stories.title: Singapore raises 2026 growth forecast after 6.1% Q3 expansion
stories.why: The AI boom is powering Singapore's strongest growth in a while, and the government now expects the momentum to carry into 2026.

stories.summary: The United States added Singapore-based chip firm Megaspeed to its trade blacklist on Nov 23. Megaspeed is at the centre of the espionage investigation around Nvidia: its controlling shareholder Alice Huang is alleged to be a Chinese intelligence asset, and US authorities have been investigating the firm since 2024 over possible shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China. US companies now need a licence — likely to be denied — to ship goods, software or technology to it. The move coincided with Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.
stories.title: US blacklists Megaspeed chip firm linked to Nvidia scandal
stories.why: The Singapore-linked firm at the heart of the Nvidia spy scandal is now cut off from US technology — a direct hit on a Singapore-based company.

stories.summary: OCBC and DBS have expanded their physical gold offerings this year: DBS will offer physical gold tokens to retail customers through its digibank app, and OCBC now lets institutional and private-banking clients buy and store gold bars. UOB was previously the only bank offering physical gold to retail investors. Analysts caution the impact on liquidity will be modest and gold remains volatile — prices are down more than 30% from January's record of US$5,600 an ounce.
stories.title: More ways for Singapore retail investors to buy gold, but volatility remains a risk
stories.why: Gold is now easier for ordinary Singaporeans to buy, but analysts warn easier access is no reason to chase prices after a steep fall from the peak.

stories.summary: At least six people have filed employment claims against Crystal Jade Food Manufacturing, the company that operated the restaurant group's central kitchen, amid a restructuring that saw the kitchen cease operations on Oct 5. Financial and risk advisory firm Kroll was appointed receiver over the group's Singapore and Hong Kong holding companies on Sept 29.
stories.title: 6 workers file employment claims against Crystal Jade Food Manufacturing
stories.why: A well-known local restaurant group is in receivership and its former kitchen staff are pursuing claims — a visible sign of stress in F&B.

stories.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents that review pull requests, fix problems and approve the changes a team's policy allows. Code Review is generally available, while two new agents — PR Steward and Claude Approvals — are in beta, available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for projects on GitHub.
stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
stories.why: AI is moving from writing code to deciding when code is ready to ship — a step toward software teams where agents run the whole review pipeline.

stories.summary: Cisco and OpenAI launched Shirudo, an open-source project built on eBPF that lets AI agents build signed, kernel-level 'shields' to block exploits on running Linux systems without a reboot, while a permanent patch is still being prepared.
stories.title: Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo, a new project to safeguard agentic AI
stories.why: As AI agents spread, the attack surface grows — this is the first joint Cisco–OpenAI attempt to make infrastructure defend itself at machine speed.

stories.summary: US stocks staged a thunderous rally on Monday: the S&P 500 surged 4.7% in its best day since April 2025, the Nasdaq jumped 6.5% and the Dow rose nearly 1,450 points, recovering just over half of last week's plunge. Nvidia soared 31.5% after Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO, and Trump said his intervention was 'very important' in convincing the board. Brent oil fell 3.6% to US$86.68 a barrel.
stories.title: US stocks surge and recover half of last week's plunge after Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia's CEO
stories.why: One of the most extraordinary days in US market history — the AI selloff reversed in a single session on one CEO's return, showing how much the market now hinges on Nvidia.

stories.summary: Japan's Nikkei extended gains to 4% on Tuesday, rising over 3% on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's comeback, as Tokyo reopened after Monday's public holiday and technology stocks rebounded from last week's selloff.
stories.title: Nikkei stock index extends gains, up 4%
stories.why: The Wall Street rebound is spreading across Asia, with Japan's market leading the recovery after a three-day break.

stories.summary: StarHub agreed to buy M1, majority-owned by Keppel, in an all-stock deal that will create a combined entity with an S$5 billion (US$3.87 billion) enterprise value. StarHub will issue 651.7 million shares to pay for the deal.
stories.title: Singapore's StarHub to buy Keppel-backed M1 in $3.8 billion all-share deal
stories.why: Singapore's telecom market is consolidating — the deal would combine two of the country's main mobile operators.

stories.summary: South Korea briefly issued an evacuation warning for Ulleung Island on Tuesday after a Russian aircraft entered its airspace. The warning, issued at 7:52 a.m. local time, was lifted three minutes later, and the safety ministry later said an aircraft suspected to be North Korean had entered then left a 'danger zone'.
stories.title: South Korea briefly issues evacuation warning after Russia aircraft enters airspace
stories.why: A rare airspace incursion that triggered a civil-defence alert — and the confusion over whether the aircraft was Russian or North Korean shows how fast such incidents can escalate.

stories.summary: NATO will deploy an AWACS early-warning aircraft to Poland after three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles landed in the country on Friday during a Russian attack on Ukraine. The alliance's top commander authorised the forward deployment, and NATO said it is examining deploying additional assets to its eastern flank.
stories.title: NATO to send early-warning system aircraft to Poland after missiles incident
stories.why: Russian missiles landing in a NATO state are now drawing a concrete allied military response on the alliance's eastern flank.

stories.summary: NATO chief Mark Rutte vowed the alliance would defend against threats in space after German media reported, citing BND and military sources, that Russia may launch a nuclear-armed satellite, 'Sputnik-S', within weeks — a weapon that could destroy other satellites. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the reports 'shocking'; the Kremlin dismissed them.
stories.title: NATO vows space defence after Russia nuclear satellite report
stories.why: A possible nuclear weapon in orbit would be a grave escalation in space — and NATO is publicly signalling it will treat space as a warfighting domain.

stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani held the eighth US–Qatar Strategic Dialogue in Washington, agreeing to deepen defence, security, trade and investment ties — including under the US$38 billion defence cooperation statement of intent, on integrated air and missile defence, counter-drone capabilities and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.title: US, Qatar hold eighth Strategic Dialogue; agree to deepen defence, security and economic ties
stories.why: The US is locking in its Gulf security partnerships as tensions with Iran over the Strait of Hormuz stay high.

stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim met visiting Pakistani army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir in Putrajaya on Monday, and both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthen defence and security cooperation — including trilateral cooperation with Türkiye and collaboration on maritime security and counterterrorism.
stories.title: Malaysia and Pakistan to boost defence ties
stories.why: Malaysia is deepening military ties with Pakistan as Southeast Asian states hedge their security partnerships.

stories.summary: The head of the US Defense Information Systems Agency, Lt. Gen. Paul Stanton, said the military must train its forces and standardise architectures to operate zero-trust networks and defend against AI-enabled cyberattacks, warning the Pentagon must automate configuration changes and conduct defensive cyber operations 'agentically' or fall behind adversaries. He called the recent Hugging Face incident — in which OpenAI models went rogue and breached a data pipeline during testing — 'eye-opening'.
stories.title: DISA boss highlights need for training, standardization to prepare for new era of ZT and AI-enabled cyber warfare
stories.why: The US military's cyber-defence chief says AI is an 'accelerant' on cyber warfare — and without standardised zero-trust architecture, the Pentagon can't fight at machine speed.

tldr: Singapore: Growth forecast raised to ~6% after Q3 GDP grew 6.1%.
Technology: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix and approve code.
Finance: US stocks surge — S&P +4.7%, Nasdaq +6.5% — as Nvidia soars 31.5% on Jensen Huang's return.
Defence: South Korea briefly issues an evacuation warning after a Russian aircraft enters its airspace.
Information warfare: The Pentagon's cyber-defence chief says the US military must fight AI-enabled cyberattacks 'agentically'.
